topic: Projective copula-excitation frontier for scale-erased causal discovery. Fix p and an invariant acyclic linear-Gaussian SCM with unknown baseline innovation variances. Across environments, innovation coordinates receive known positive multipliers, but each site releases only its Gaussian copula/correlation matrix, with unrelated marginal scales. Define the projective Cholesky fiber of compatible directed supports. Prove the sharp universal generic criterion: every pair of multiplier-profile columns is projectively distinct iff every DAG is generically a singleton of this fiber; give explicit nonisomorphic fork/chain twins when profiles tie. Construct canonical order predictors and exact fiber recovery, including an O(Ep^3) conditional-pair algorithm on generic complete DAGs, then invert Kendall-tau rank summaries into honest graph confidence sets under explicit separation. Consumer: FedCDH-style federated summary sharing and the backShift workflow, which can accept rank-only site releases exactly above the excitation boundary. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Reference-environment Cholesky normalization was derived to eliminate continuous scale search: each candidate order determines one canonical standardized recursive model and predicts every other correlation matrix. Reversed-edge polynomial witnesses give an all-p generic uniqueness spine under pairwise nonproportional schedule columns; tied columns yield an explicit positive fork/chain counterfamily. Exact computations recovered all 25 labeled three-node DAGs across 300 rational parameter choices, checked diagonal-gauge equivariance and weak/singular regimes, and verified conditional-pair peeling through p=6. No direct primary-source or internal collision was found. Compressed standard claims, the all-p polynomial argument, sparse-graph computation, and the uniform inference perturbation layer still require independent audit. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform Cholesky-predictor perturbation bounds and close the finite-sample graph-confidence theorem with an explicit fallback convention and normalized beta-min margin. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the canonical-order reduction under arbitrary positive reference rescaling and reproduce the p=3 covariance example with d_1=(1,4,9) and all five wrong-order exclusions; any legal model outside the canonical list or matching wrong order stops this spine. open_problems.why_unsolved: BACKSHIFT's covariance differences and GnIES's likelihood and equivalence arguments retain marginal-variance information, while independent site standardizations introduce a separate positive diagonal gauge in every environment. FedCDH confirms the relevance of summary sharing, but its covariance tensors are richer than rank-only releases. Existing results therefore do not determine whether known excitation schedules cancel those gauges exactly when their columns are pairwise nonproportional, or whether every tied pair necessarily permits nonisomorphic observational twins.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient generic characterization of the projective Cholesky fiber, including an algebraic exceptional set under distinct profiles and an explicit positive-parameter fork/chain counterfamily whenever two profiles are proportional.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature controls rank-based correlation inputs or inverts order-level tests, while the prior BACKSHIFT and LiMVAM proposals explicitly leave uniform contraction and wrong-order stability unresolved. A projective predictor additionally composes Schur complements, inverses, triangular solves, diagonal normalizations, and maxima over environments and orders. Its modulus can diverge as an eigenvalue or excitation separation vanishes, so existing Kendall bounds cannot be transferred mechanically. Coverage requires simultaneous perturbation control on a normalized parameter class and a measurable fallback when an empirical matrix leaves the certified region.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A deterministic uniform predictor inequality with explicit dependence on eigenvalue, dimension, and projective separation, combined with a computable rank-based graph confidence set having at least 1−α coverage over a normalized beta-min class and a full-fiber fallback outside the certified event.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing unknown-target results exploit full densities, conditional invariances, recovered exogenous signals, or covariance magnitudes. With only correlations, the unknown excitation matrix is confounded with environment-specific marginal standardizations, and even its column magnitudes are not intrinsically defined. The missing first step is an orbit analysis that separates identifiable projective schedule directions from diagonal-gauge transformations before graph-search or target-matching arguments can apply.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint-equivalence characterization for DAG and positive-multiplier-matrix pairs that specifies the maximal identifiable quotient and gives either generic rank-and-diversity conditions for joint recovery or matched counterexamples proving impossibility.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The LiMVAM removed-set dynamic program is path-independent at the covariance-state level but can still visit factorially many order paths before deduplicating coefficient tuples. Complete-DAG conditional-pair peeling does not settle sparse graphs, where missing edges allow many orders to encode one support. The first proof step that must change is to replace residual-cross-block states with hashable projective-correlation Cholesky fragments and prove a local congruence under which two partial orders have exactly the same continuation outputs.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior BACKSHIFT proposal counts affine-line occupancy for unknown raw shift amplitudes and records only a coarse environment lower bound plus selected support examples. Known multiplicative schedules observed through correlations require a different combinatorial object: every two schedule columns must retain a nonzero projective minor after deletions, while strict positivity prevents direct reuse of binary separating codes. The first proof step changes from bounding affine incidences to packing positive projective codewords under a row-sparsity constraint.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior BACKSHIFT sufficiency argument permits positive-semidefinite invariant noise, but its necessity witness perturbs inside the positive-definite cone and does not characterize fixed singular strata. Projective Cholesky normalization is more delicate because zero innovations can produce zero pivots and erase structural distinctions from correlations. The first existing proof step that fails is the open-cone perturbation used to preserve legal positive-definite covariances while constructing a competing normalized explanation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A rank-stratified necessary-and-sufficient generic recovery characterization for each zero-innovation pattern, with explicit legal nonisomorphic twins on every nonidentifiable stratum and a closure convention for singular correlation inputs.

literature_map:
Rothenhäusler et al. (2015, BACKSHIFT) identify linear cyclic systems with latent variables from full covariance differences by joint diagonalization; their diversity condition is the closest covariance-level frontier.
Peters and Bühlmann (2014) identify Gaussian DAGs under equal error variances through recursive conditional-variance structure, anchoring Cholesky and order arguments.
Gamella et al. (2024, GnIES) characterize interventional equivalence under unknown variance interventions but retain complete environment distributions and their scales.
Li et al. (2024, FedCDH) establish the relevance of federated heterogeneous summaries, although their covariance tensors disclose more than sitewise ranks or correlations.
Yang, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (2024) separate recovery of changed exogenous noises from matching those changes to observed variables.
Squires, Wang, and Uhler (2020, UT-IGSP) address unknown intervention targets through invariances that arbitrary marginal rescaling need not preserve.
Liu et al. (2012, nonparanormal SKEPTIC) supply the standard Kendall-tau-to-latent-correlation map and uniform entrywise control.
Mitra and Zhang (2014) strengthen rank-correlation control to spectral and simultaneous-submatrix deviations, which are relevant to Schur complements.
Ghoshal and Honorio (2018) and Li, Shen, and Pan (2023) show how local precision or regression certificates yield polynomial-time Gaussian-DAG peeling.
Gao, Tai, and Aragam (2022) establish sparse Gaussian-DAG sample-complexity benchmarks under equal variances or a known order.
Wu and Drton (2023) characterize equivalence under partial homoscedasticity, suggesting a local-reversal language for fibers created by tied profiles.
Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2025) build confidence sets for causal orderings; Strieder et al. (2021) retain graph uncertainty through test inversion.
The scan found Gaussian-copula methods for rank-based Markov-equivalence recovery but no primary source characterizing known-excitation, multi-environment DAG fibers from correlation-only releases.
The central tension is that covariance-shift methods exploit precisely the marginal-scale information that federated rank-only disclosure removes.
